BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Bottom line:** Almost every position in the Seller's package departs from our playbook, several materially. Do not accept the package as presented. Two items need a decision from Amelia Frost before we respond: the cap and the claims period.

---

## 1. Threshold point: the Seller's framing does not bind us

The covering material tries to narrow our review:

- Most clauses are tagged **[STANDARD]**.
- Positions are described as "settled at principal level" and "FINAL".
- A "Reviewer Efficiency Note" asks that only **[OPEN]** items be reviewed. Nothing in the package is actually marked [OPEN].
- It asserts that we "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

**My approach:** I have reviewed every clause against our playbook. The labels and the efficiency note are the counterparty's drafting, not agreed terms.

**Why the claims don't hold up:**

- **No authority on file.** Nothing on our side records any principal-level agreement. Our playbook says Amelia Frost has given no authority for the 20% cap or the 18-month period.
- **The document contradicts itself.** It calls itself an "Update draft" and invites our mark-up, yet claims the terms are closed.
- **"Market" assertions are unverified.** The ranges quoted (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge bars) are the Seller's characterisation. They don't displace our positions.

**Recommended action:** Ask Amelia Frost directly whether she agreed anything with Harbourglass. Unless she confirms in writing, our response should state plainly that no limitation, disclosure or knowledge terms have been agreed and that all clauses remain open.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability architecture

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None given. | High |
| 2 | De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Medium |
| 3 | Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded | High |
| 4 | General claims period (cl 12.3) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's approval. None given. | High |
| 5 | "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" (cl 12.3/13) | Global default | No hidden override of Title, Tax, IP, payment or covenant categories | High |
| 6 | Title / capacity | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Critical |
| 7 | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | No fraud carve-out | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable. Not waivable. | Critical |

**Reasoning:**

- **Items 1 and 4.** We cannot move to the fallback positions without authority. Even with authority, we should only trade them for real concessions elsewhere.
- **Items 2 and 3.** The thresholds work together. A AUD 25k per-claim floor plus a AUD 250k deductible-style basket screens out a large band of genuine loss. The "excess only" mechanic is a deductible, not a tipping basket. That is a separate departure from our position, beyond the dollar figures.
- **Item 5 is the most dangerous drafting point, because it is quiet.** Applying limitations to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" makes the general regime the default for everything. That includes specific indemnities (Ironquay), title, tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants. Any category we fail to carve out expressly falls into the 20% cap, 18 months and the AUD 250k basket.
  - **Response:** Reverse it. General limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Each other category has its own stated regime.
- **Item 6.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m share purchase. If title fails, we have bought nothing. This is non-negotiable.
- **Item 7.** As drafted, the Seller could rely on the cap, time bar and non-reliance clause even for fraud. Our playbook says no one may waive the carve-out.
  - Insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct across caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
  - Have NSW counsel confirm the drafting reaches "the maximum extent enforceable."

### B. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**8. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]).** Reject.

- The Seller discloses everything in the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 and beyond), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- This defeats the warranties: any fact buried anywhere in the data room is deemed disclosed.
- **Response:**
  - Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail for us to assess the nature and scope of the matter.
  - Delete [1.1] and [1.2], or limit them to documents expressly referenced in a specific disclosure.
  - Confirm that [1.4] (non-admission) cannot be used to dilute any warranty or indemnity.

**9. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** Delete. This is the clause most likely to hollow out our protection.

- It bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- Combined with the Disclosure Letter, it would arguably bar claims on exactly the known problems: Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, the bonuses and the Sandbar renewals. Those are the matters we most need protection on.
- **Fallback, only if the Seller insists on a qualifier:**
  - Knowledge is limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry. That is a Seller-knowledge qualifier, not a buyer bar.
  - It never excuses title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### C. Conditions and completion deliverables

**10. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3).**

- The Disclosure Letter ([2]) confirms the facts:
  - Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m).
  - Its contract has a change-control clause (11.2) with conditions in 11.3.
  - No final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied have been provided.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, and treats the condition as satisfied as soon as a consent letter is delivered. That ignores the 11.3 conditions and leaves the Seller with an endeavours-only obligation on a material customer.
- **Response:** A condition precedent requiring:
  - an effective written consent under cl 11.2; and
  - documentary evidence that every cl 11.3 condition is satisfied, before Completion.
- The condition should be waivable by the Buyer only, with an appropriate long-stop date.
- Reasonable endeavours is insufficient. At minimum the Seller should carry a strengthened obligation and a Buyer walk right if the condition fails.

**11. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7).**

- The Disclosure Letter ([3]) confirms ~AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is provided.
- A release "following Completion" means we would complete with live security over the target, and possibly a change-control default triggered by our own acquisition.
- **Response:**
  - A current payout letter.
  - Repayment directly to Riverlark from Completion funds, treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free price.
  - Executed security releases (including any PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion.
- A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

**12. Employee bonuses (funds flow).**

- The Disclosure Letter ([5]) confirms AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses (DD-005). They are not in the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed.
- Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow is the silent exclusion our playbook warns against. If the Company owes them, we bear them post-Completion unless they are dealt with.
- **Response:** Either:
  - a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt or Transaction Costs, covering the bonuses plus all triggered on-costs; or
  - express Seller funding backed by an indemnity.
- Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs. We should not assume a figure.

### D. Specific risk matters

**13. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).**

- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As the Seller itself concedes, that is not independent verification. There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers only the fee. It does not cover the real risk: that the Company does not own the SOW3 materials, together with any third-party claims, remediation or re-development costs.
- **Response:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights in, the SOW3 Project Materials.
  - Preserve the cure: Seller procures cleared payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally before Completion.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.
  - Don't treat AUD 180,000 as the confirmed figure in either direction.

**14. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6).**

- The Seller's summary says it is "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter ([6]) is more careful:
  - about 1,240 records were potentially exposed via a link sent to an unintended external address;
  - access, scope and any notification obligation are unestablished;
  - the investigation is preliminary.
- We should not accept "not material." Equally, we should not assert a breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure. None is established.
- **Response:** Pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller and Company to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link and the recipient's position;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings;
  - consult the Buyer before any regulator or customer communication.
- Pair these with a warranty on the accuracy of the disclosed facts. Consider whether to seek specific indemnity protection depending on what the investigation shows.

**15. Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011, AUD 330,000).**

- The Seller asserts "ordinary course." The Disclosure Letter ([8]) is more neutral: it says the three AUD 110k renewals should be read together and doesn't say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Our playbook says assess, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. We don't concede "ordinary course" either.
- **Response:** Request the contracts and the approval trail, and assess term, termination rights, accrual and whether the three are linked. Decide treatment once we have the facts. Reserve the position in our mark-up.

**16. Tax / IP regime.**

- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." Our playbook treats Tax and IP as **OPEN**.
- **Response:** Reject the characterisation. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own (to be negotiated) caps and periods. We are not assuming unlimited liability, and we are not assuming any position is resolved.

**17. Title evidence (DD-012).**

- The Seller relies on its own share register. As the Disclosure Letter ([10]) itself notes, that is the source relied on, not verification. Our playbook treats DD-012 as an internal source, not independent proof.
- **Response:** Require independent evidence, for example:
  - a current ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and shares;
  - the constitution, plus any pre-emption waivers;
  - Seller board approvals and authority to sell;
  - confirmation of no encumbrances.
- Back this with title and capacity warranties under the separate fundamental regime (item 6).

**18. Minor items: office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).**

- The Disclosure Letter describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not share-sale consents.
- **Response:** Confirm by our own review of the underlying documents. Add any landlord notification to the completion deliverables and covenants.

---

## 3. A useful asymmetry

The Seller's covering summary consistently softens what its own Disclosure Letter says:

| Matter | Covering summary | Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "Addressed" | No consent; conditions unevidenced |
| DD-006 | "Not expected to be material" | Scope and access unestablished |
| Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Not stated |

We should quote the Disclosure Letter back to the Seller in our mark-up. Its own disclosures support every one of our completion and indemnity asks.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright (non-negotiable under the playbook):**

1. Any limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance term without a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
2. Title and capacity under the general cap and period. Insist on a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
3. Whole-data-room, Accounts, statutory register and public-record general disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
4. The blanket buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3). Delete it.
5. The "limitations apply to all Claims" default. Confine general limitations to general Warranty Claims.

**Counter with our starting positions:**

6. Cap at 25% / AUD 6.0m. De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar). Claims period 24 months.
7. Tax and IP remain open, separate categories.

**Completion mechanics:**

8. Bluefen: a condition precedent for effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, waivable by the Buyer only.
9. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and security releases at Completion.
10. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
11. Title: independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, approvals), not just DD-012.

**Specific protections and diligence:**

12. Ironquay: a broadened ownership indemnity, with the payment and confirmatory-assignment cure preserved, outside the general regime.
13. DD-006: covenants on preservation, investigation, updates and consultation. Take no position on breach or materiality yet.
14. Sandbar: request information and reserve treatment. No automatic Debt classification, and no concession that the renewals are ordinary course.
15. Lease and Mossvale: confirm by our own review and add any notifications to the deliverables.

**Internal actions before we respond:**

- **Amelia Frost:** confirm whether any principal-level agreement exists. Note that no authority has been given for the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks. Riverlark post-completion release approval would also be needed if that route is ever proposed.
- **Covering note to the Seller:** state that we do not accept the [STANDARD]/FINAL designations or the "accepted framework" statement, and that the full agreement remains under negotiation.

- **Response:** A condition precedent requiring:
  - an effective written consent under cl 11.2; and
  - documentary evidence that every cl 11.3 condition is satisfied, before Completion.
- The condition should be waivable by the Buyer only, with an appropriate long-stop date.
- Reasonable endeavours is insufficient. At minimum the Seller should carry a strengthened obligation and a Buyer walk right if the condition fails.

**11. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7).**

- The Disclosure Letter ([3]) confirms ~AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is provided.
- A release "following Completion" means we would complete with live security over the target, and possibly a change-control default triggered by our own acquisition.
- **Response:**
  - A current payout letter.
  - Repayment directly to Riverlark from Completion funds, treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free price.
  - Executed security releases (including any PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion.
- A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

**12. Employee bonuses (funds flow).**

- The Disclosure Letter ([5]) confirms AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses (DD-005). They are not in the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed.
- Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow is the silent exclusion our playbook warns against. If the Company owes them, we bear them post-Completion unless they are dealt with.
- **Response:** Either:
  - a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt or Transaction Costs, covering the bonuses plus all triggered on-costs; or
  - express Seller funding backed by an indemnity.
- Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs. We should not assume a figure.

### D. Specific risk matters

**13. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).**

- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As the Seller itself concedes, that is not independent verification. There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers only the fee. It does not cover the real risk: that the Company does not own the SOW3 materials, together with any third-party claims, remediation or re-development costs.
- **Response:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights in, the SOW3 Project Materials.
  - Preserve the cure: Seller procures cleared payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally before Completion.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.
  - Don't treat AUD 180,000 as the confirmed figure in either direction.

**14. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6).**

- The Seller's summary says it is "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter ([6]) is more careful:
  - about 1,240 records were potentially exposed via a link sent to an unintended external address;
  - access, scope and any notification obligation are unestablished;
  - the investigation is preliminary.
- We should not accept "not material." Equally, we should not assert a breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure. None is established.
- **Response:** Pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller and Company to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link and the recipient's position;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings;
  - consult the Buyer before any regulator or customer communication.
- Pair these with a warranty on the accuracy of the disclosed facts. Consider whether to seek specific indemnity protection depending on what the investigation shows.

**15. Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011, AUD 330,000).**

- The Seller asserts "ordinary course." The Disclosure Letter ([8]) is more neutral: it says the three AUD 110k renewals should be read together and doesn't say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Our playbook says assess, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. We don't concede "ordinary course" either.
- **Response:** Request the contracts and the approval trail, and assess term, termination rights, accrual and whether the three are linked. Decide treatment once we have the facts. Reserve the position in our mark-up.

**16. Tax / IP regime.**

- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." Our playbook treats Tax and IP as **OPEN**.
- **Response:** Reject the characterisation. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own (to be negotiated) caps and periods. We are not assuming unlimited liability, and we are not assuming any position is resolved.

**17. Title evidence (DD-012).**

- The Seller relies on its own share register. As the Disclosure Letter ([10]) itself notes, that is the source relied on, not verification. Our playbook treats DD-012 as an internal source, not independent proof.
- **Response:** Require independent evidence, for example:
  - a current ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and shares;
  - the constitution, plus any pre-emption waivers;
  - Seller board approvals and authority to sell;
  - confirmation of no encumbrances.
- Back this with title and capacity warranties under the separate fundamental regime (item 6).

**18. Minor items: office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).**

- The Disclosure Letter describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not share-sale consents.
- **Response:** Confirm by our own review of the underlying documents. Add any landlord notification to the completion deliverables and covenants.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright (non-negotiable under the playbook):**

1. Any limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance term without a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
2. Title and capacity under the general cap and period. Insist on a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
3. Whole-data-room, Accounts, statutory register and public-record general disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
4. The blanket buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3). Delete it.
5. The "limitations apply to all Claims" default. Confine general limitations to general Warranty Claims.

**Counter with our starting positions:**

6. Cap at 25% / AUD 6.0m. De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar). Claims period 24 months.
7. Tax and IP remain open, separate categories.

**Completion mechanics:**

8. Bluefen: a condition precedent for effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, waivable by the Buyer only.
9. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and security releases at Completion.
10. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
11. Title: independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, approvals), not just DD-012.

**Specific protections and diligence:**

12. Ironquay: a broadened ownership indemnity, with the payment and confirmatory-assignment cure preserved, outside the general regime.
13. DD-006: covenants on preservation, investigation, updates and consultation. Take no position on breach or materiality yet.
14. Sandbar: request information and reserve treatment. No automatic Debt classification, and no concession that the renewals are ordinary course.
15. Lease and Mossvale: confirm by our own review and add any notifications to the deliverables.

**Internal actions before we respond:**

- **Amelia Frost:** confirm whether any principal-level agreement exists. Note that no authority has been given for the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks. Riverlark post-completion release approval would also be needed if that route is ever proposed.
- **Covering note to the Seller:** state that we do not accept the [STANDARD]/FINAL designations or the "accepted framework" statement, and that the full agreement remains under negotiation.
